name: connective tissue disease overview
title: Connective tissue diseases: the signature feature sorts lupus and antiphospholipid syndrome, Sjogren's syndrome, inflammatory myositis and systemic sclerosis; each column gives presentation, the antibodies and tests in order, and treatment, with Raynaud's and lupus care below

root.title: Woman, several organs, often Raynaud's: which connective tissue disease?
lines: all more common in women · most are antinuclear antibody (ANA) positive
ANA negative → lupus highly unlikely · ANA positive alone proves nothing (common in the healthy)

groups.title: Rash in the sun, mouth ulcers, organs, or CLOTS

head: h
Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
1 in 1000 · women 9:1 · young
pres: • malar rash (spares the nasolabial folds), discoid, photosensitive
• mouth or nose ulcers · non-erosive arthritis
tx: the anchor: skin, joints, fewer flares
Major organ → high-dose steroid + immune suppressant

head: h
Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS)
half with SLE · in 10-20% of SLE
h
Sjögren's syndrome
2 in 10,000 · lymphocytes in exocrine glands
pres: • gritty eyes, worse through the day

head: h
Inflammatory myositis
1 in 100,000 · shoulders, hips, neck
pres: • children, older adults · may be cancer
any age · NO rash · not cancer-linked

head: h
Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma)
1 in 10,000 · highest mortality
tx: Renal crisis: blood pressure ↑, hemolysis, kidneys fail
methotrexate softens skin in early diffuse

panels.title: Raynaud's: primary or secondary?
items: primary: no disease, often no drug needed
Raynaud's + dilated nailfold capillaries + anticentromere → ⅓ get scleroderma in 5 years

panels.title: Every lupus patient
items: sun avoidance, SPF 30 · cardiovascular risk (50× events)
die of cardiovascular events, infection, SLE, drug complications
